turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Observations are done. Blood pressure was a hundred and fifty-two over eighty-eight, pulse seventy-eight, temperature thirty-six point eight. He says he's fine, of course.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I am fine. It's a toe. I don't know why we've all trooped in.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come and sit down, both of you. I'm glad you're here. What's been going on with you?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing much. Um, the big toe's a bit sore, that's all. Hardly worth a doctor's time.
[SEG0005] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Nothing much, he says. He was hopping round the kitchen at two this morning, Derek.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Oh, that sounds horrid. When did it actually start?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Went to bed right as rain, and then in the night it just started to...
[SEG0008] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Throb. You were swearing at two o'clock. I know because you woke me.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, alright. Since last night, then. It'll wear off.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is it swollen, or just sore?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): A touch puffy, if you stare at it. You're both fussing.
[SEG0012] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's the left big toe, and it's enormous, red and hot. He wouldn't let the sheet so much as touch it.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any of the other joints joined in? Knees, ankles, the other foot?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Just that toe. Rest of me's perfectly fine.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): And have you felt feverish, or shivery?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry, I was miles away. What?
[SEG0017] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She means a temperature, love.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No temperature, no shivers. I'm not ill.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Could you have knocked it on something?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No injury. I haven't kicked anything.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Hang on, though, that's not quite...
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): No rush. What are you remembering?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Yesterday evening, getting up from tea, I caught the chair leg with that toe. Proper kick. Didn't hurt at the time so I binned the thought.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right, so there was a knock after all. Has this toe ever flared like this before?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Once. Same business. Went away on its own, so I didn't make a song and dance.
[SEG0026] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A year back. You were hobbling the best part of a week and still telling everyone it was a twinge.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): A year back, yeah, something like that. They did take blood, I remember that much.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you remember what they told you about that blood test?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Fellow said the uric acid was borderline. Didn't give me any tablets, so it can't have mattered.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about medicines you take regularly?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Just the water tablet. For my blood pressure. Been on that for years, nothing else.
[SEG0032] person_1 (NURSE): I've got bendroflumethiazide on the repeat list, two point five milligrams, once a day.
[SEG0033] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's out of date. They put it up to five milligrams, back in March. I collect them, so I do know.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Five, two and a half... I just swallow the one tablet. I don't study the box.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): How about alcohol? I'm thinking beer, wine, that sort of thing.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Weekends I'll have a few pints. Well, actually, not every weekend, but most. Not in the week.
[SEG0037] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's fair. Saturdays and Sundays, and he leaves it alone on weekdays.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Completely different thing, did you see they nearly called the county game off?
[SEG0039] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We drove past the ground. Traffic was diabolical, forty minutes on the ring road, barely moved.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): I saw that queue from the top of the bus. Was it raining on you as well?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Spitting, on and off. And my grandson's beside himself, he's wicketkeeper for the under-thirteens on Sunday.
[SEG0042] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Won't take the new gloves off in the house. Bright blue. If it tips down they'll abandon the final, and he'll be heartbroken.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Oh I hope it stays dry for him. Lovely thing, that age.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Taller than his mum already, would you believe. Anyway, you were saying.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, let's see the foot, if the shoe will come off without a fight.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): There. Bit pink. I've had worse sunburn.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): The left big toe is red and warm, and the joint at the base is swollen and very tender to press. Ankle and the other toes look completely ordinary.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Well if you press it, obviously. Left alone it's manageable.

[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): I hear you playing it down, but I think this is most likely an acute attack of gout. Night coming on suddenly, that red hot joint, weekend beer, and a water tablet all point the same way. It's a working impression, mind, not something I can stamp as certain until we see the bloods.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Gout. That's old men and port, isn't it. It'll be gone by the morning.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): It may ease, but I'd still like to treat it. I'll start colchicine, five hundred micrograms by mouth, twice a day, for five days, for this flare.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Tablets as well? Seems over the top.

[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'd really rather you took them. If the colchicine disagrees with your stomach, we might switch you to naproxen, five hundred milligrams twice a day, plus a stomach-protecting tablet. Only if you can't manage the colchicine, not today.
[SEG0054] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What about that blood test they did before, the borderline one?

[SEG0055] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll arrange a fresh blood uric acid this afternoon, and kidney function at the same time, because of the colchicine and the water tablet. No point guessing off an old borderline result.

[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): Please keep taking the water tablet, don't stop it on your own. Cut the weekend pints back while the toe is angry, and rest the foot up. Come and see me in a week so we can look at the toe and those bloods. If it's worse before then, or you feel properly unwell, don't sit on it, ring us or come back sooner.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): A week is plenty. It'll have sorted itself, but I'll come if it keeps you happy.
